Vector Splatting visualizes vector fields by embedding direction indicators into scalar reconstruction texture maps, allowing the simultaneous rendering of scalar density and vector direction [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that Vector Splatting visualizes vector fields by embedding direction indicators into scalar reconstruction texture maps, allowing simultaneous rendering of scalar density and vector direction. Source [S1] explicitly supports this in the section 'Combined Vector and Scalar Textures', stating: 'We can integrate vector fields into the scalar reconstruction function... The splat is rendered using a portion of Figure 3a as an intensity map, and the same portion of Figure 3b for an opacity map... This function will give us colored vectors, with the appropriately colored splats, both of which are attenuated by the polygon's opacity.' It further confirms that the scalar field is 'adequately represented' while the 'additional vector field can easily be noted' (Results section). The mechanism of embedding direction indicators (via rotation and texture mapping) into the reconstruction process is clearly described.
